title: Simplify Companion current-proposal authority and projection repair

verify.basis: Fresh task-scoped PostgreSQL, migration, lifecycle, concurrency, projection repair/rollback, HTTP/read, access/feed, exact-head, and static boundary evidence passed without reusing execute receipts.
verify.next_owner: Run per-task /red-verify, then obtain HUMAN_CHECKPOINT: done before explicit-owner or scheduler closure; task remains in_progress.

evidence_required: Forward migration and ORM inspection proving that current_proposal_id and its cyclic FK are absent while all Issue, Attention, Proposal, DecisionRecord, UI, and Timeline authority rows remain preserved.

PostgreSQL lifecycle evidence proving that active current proposal is derived from the unique pending row linked by proposal.attention_id, supersede reuses an unchanged attention, and same-run/distinct-run concurrency semantics remain intact.

Projection evidence proving that stale or missing proposal UI presentation is rebuilt from authoritative proposal state during supersede while actual projection persistence or Timeline failure still rolls back the UoW.

HTTP/read evidence proving unchanged public schemas, derived current_proposal_ref, strict serialization, no projection fallback, retained authorization, and no Farm/Plant existence leak on supported application paths.
All current exact-head consumers advanced from ft012_simplify_follow_up_runtime to ft013_simplify_companion without rewriting applied migrations.

Current-attempt T3 protocol evidence with fresh functional verification, /verify VERDICT: PASS, per-task /red-verify SEMANTIC_VERDICT: semantic-pass, and the exact HUMAN_CHECKPOINT: done marker before explicit-owner or scheduler closure.
purpose: Reduce the implemented FT-013 W1 aggregate to one-way proposal authority before DecisionRecord work: remove the redundant attention-to-current-proposal pointer, derive the current proposal from existing PostgreSQL uniqueness, make presentation repair authority-derived, and preserve all supported public and safety behavior.
success_outcome: The backend persists and reads the same Plant-scoped IssueStack/proposal lifecycle with unchanged HTTP schemas, authorization, archive behavior, idempotency, concurrency, Timeline, and Safety boundaries, while active current proposal identity comes only from the unique pending CompanionProposal linked to the active attention, supersede leaves that attention unchanged, and stale or missing proposal UI projection is rebuilt from proposal authority rather than vetoing the transition.
anti_goals: Do not reopen or rewrite TASK-041 history, its applied aggregate migration, or its terminal evidence.
Do not implement TASK-042 DecisionRecord, decision/close commands, ordinary-task effects, DecisionRecord Bus/context, or binding decision projections.
Do not implement TASK-043 Companion provider/runtime invocation, production router registration, provider selection, external egress, or live smoke.
Do not change public issue/detail fields, ref grammar, pagination, authorization, Plant archive/grant semantics, Safety Gate, Task authority, Plant state, device behavior, or frontend/PWA.

Do not add replacement pointer state, a materialized current-proposal read model, a new index already covered by the existing unique pending index, a worker, scheduler, outbox, or unsupported storage-repair subsystem.

forbidden_scope: TASK-042 DecisionRecord/effect/close behavior, Task source extension, Bus/context publication, or decision projection.
TASK-043 provider/runtime/orchestration, backend/app/main.py registration, external egress, provider/model selection, or credentialed smoke.
Authorization policy, Plant lifecycle, Safety approval/action Task, Plant-state mutation, device commands, automated actuation, frontend/PWA, worker, scheduler, or outbox.
Rewriting backend/migrations/versions/ft013_companion_governance_aggregate.py or synthesizing new TASK-041 verification/closure evidence.
stop_conditions: The executor-confirmed Alembic head is not ft012_simplify_follow_up_runtime or the applied aggregate shape differs materially from the linked data spec.
Removing current_proposal_id would require dropping or rewriting supported Issue, Attention, Proposal, DecisionRecord, UI, or Timeline authority rows.
The unchanged public current_proposal_ref cannot be derived from the unique pending proposal for active attention without a new stored pointer or public schema change.
Projection rebuild would require weakening visible_to_agents=false, consumable_by_agents=false, current authorization, or the owning transaction boundary.
Existing uncommitted work overlaps the aggregate migration, Companion package, or focused tests in a way that cannot be reconciled without modifying user-owned changes.

constraints: The primary owning capability is backend/app/companion_governance; repository/service code, not API handlers, generic utilities, or the composition root, owns current-proposal derivation and projection repair orchestration.

The new ft013_simplify_companion forward migration follows ft012_simplify_follow_up_runtime, drops only fk_companion_attention_current_proposal and companion_human_attention.current_proposal_id, preserves retained rows, and leaves the applied aggregate revision unchanged.
The active current proposal is the one state=pending row for the same issue and attention under uq_companion_proposals_one_pending_per_issue; no new index or stored reverse pointer is added.
Supersede locks the active attention and unique pending proposal, transitions the old proposal, creates the replacement, and does not increment attention.record_version.

Attention UI remains the immutable notification created for the cycle. Proposal terminal UI is an authority-derived overwrite/upsert that preserves strict non-agent-consumable semantics; actual write failure remains transactional.
Read queries enforce authorized Farm/Plant/issue scope and response models enforce public serialization without revalidating the complete retained governance graph.
Every exact-head assertion present after TASK-040/TASK-041 advances to the new revision in this task.
invariants: PostgreSQL Issue, Attention, Proposal, and future DecisionRecord rows remain governance authority; UI Feed and Timeline remain derived presentation/audit and cannot create or transition governance.
At most one pending proposal per issue and at most one active attention per issue remain PostgreSQL-enforced; a pending proposal must be linked to the active attention on supported write paths.
Boss/granted-Engineer write authority, Consultant retained read scope, active-Plant/archive/grant guards, and no-existence-leak behavior remain unchanged.
Proposal/model text and Companion UI rows remain non-agent-consumable; no DecisionRecord, Task, Safety, Plant-state, action, completion, Outcome, or device authority is added.
Same-run retries remain one-effect idempotent, distinct runs retain locked serialization, and restore never replays denied work.
verification_targets: Migration/model tests prove the new exact head, removed reverse column/FK, retained one-way proposal attention FK and partial uniqueness, preserved rows, and unchanged no-cascade/strict UI constraints.

PostgreSQL lifecycle tests prove initial proposal creation without a reverse pointer, unchanged attention across one or more supersedes, derived current proposal, exact retry/conflict behavior, and same-run/distinct-run concurrency.

Projection tests prove canonical overwrite/upsert of stale or missing proposal UI rows, preserved identity/timestamp and non-consumability, correct terminal state, Timeline cardinality/redaction, and rollback only for real persistence/audit failures.

HTTP tests prove unchanged OpenAPI/detail/list schemas, derived active current_proposal_ref, active-else-latest selection, strict safe errors/no-store, retained archive/Consultant reads, and no projection fallback or cross-Plant leak.
Focused Agent Chat, access, migration, Safety, Task Follow-Up, and full deterministic regressions prove no authority, public-contract, or current-head regression.
